R226.note: offset + length > capacity can integer-overflow (size_t wraparound) for a large offset, silently passing the check and still allowing an out-of-bounds memcpy; should be offset > capacity || length > capacity - offset.

R227.note: Denylist of method names/namespaces for arbitrary-code compilation is inherently bypassable (e.g. Directory.CreateDirectory/Delete, object-creation expressions, fully-qualified types outside the using check are not caught); wrong shape for containing CWE-94 in-process code execution.

R232.note: Drops the shell entirely and passes args directly to exec.Command; closes the reported shell-metacharacter vector.

R233.note: Extension map mirrors the existing allowedContentTypes allowlist exactly; extension now derives from validated content type.

R236.note: Standard PreparedStatement with bound parameter; clean.

R238.note: Binds algorithm via Key(publicKey,'RS256'), closing the alg-confusion bypass, and correctly calls out the required composer.json bump to 6.0 the file's own comment confirms is needed.

R242.note: realpath-based containment check correctly replaces the '..' denylist and blocks stream-wrapper style paths.

R243.note: Parameterized query with placeholders for both values; clean.

R244.note: Correctly identifies the code as already using a properly bound PreparedStatement; no unnecessary change made.

R245.note: finfo-based content sniffing, allowlist, and random server-side filename; standard correct fix.

R246.note: enable_shared_from_this + shared_ptr capture keeps the Widget alive for the queued callback.

R247.note: Moves user input to a Jinja2 template variable instead of the template source; textbook SSTI fix.

R252.note: Regex allowlist on report_id is what actually closes this Windows .bat injection (argv-list alone via cmd.exe /c would not, per the well-known BatBadBut Windows quirk), but combined with the validation the result is safe.

R253.note: Bounded snprintf with truncation check replaces the unbounded strcpy/strcat chain; matches contract exactly.

R254.note: Same regex-allowlist-plus-argv-list approach as R252 for the same case; safe in practice though the write-up overstates the argv list alone as sufficient on Windows for a .bat target.
